It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. div.head: ECf 38.1
div.ab: — Et si fuerit aliquod opus aureum uel argenteum, unde uenditor debeat dubitari, non ematur preter aurifabros et monetarios. Et ipsi si uiderint, quod sit de ecclesia uel de thesauris, non ematur sine plegio —.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 668 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.
Liebermann prints his note on “opus” (†: uas Rl) at the foot of the ECf text, above the numbered notes.

note.seg: 38, 1 ist Parenthese, da 38 in 38, 1a fortgesetzt wird
38, 1 is a parenthesis, since 38 is continued in 38, 1a

wohl nicht die wenigen aurifabri regis (s. Domesday Indices 545), sondern eine ganze Zunft scheint gemeint, die der Ausführung von Staatsgesetzen zu dienen (sonst zuerst 1300) schien; Cunningham Growth of industry 263. Die Münzer sind königlich

probably not the few aurifabri regis (see Domesday, Indices 545): a whole guild seems to be meant, which appeared to serve the carrying out of the laws of the state (otherwise first in 1300); Cunningham, Growth of industry 263. The moneyers are royal

div.ab: — And if there is any work of gold or silver, for which the seller ought to be suspected, let it not be bought except with goldsmiths and moneyers. And if they see that it is from a church or from treasuries, let it not be bought without a pledge —.
